Record session traces
Record session traces
Merge the three cleanup streams: native, jbmc and examples
Cleanup Phase 4, step 2: the 18 run records published under their sessions' traces, with check at 0 errors
Cleanup Phase 4, step 3: the merge's examples 150-152, 160-161, 170-172 and 190-196 and lib/tests/integration.rs queued at the merge (verification pending)
prune_workspaces.py: delete jj workspaces only once nothing in them can be lost
Record verification results for the cleanup merge's 4 jobs, all passed
prune_workspaces.py only reports, and prints the delete command for a person to run
Cleanup Phase 4, step 4: the merge's four jobs passed, and the for-review list names every entry's state: the cleanup loop is done
Record session traces
The cleanup loop's for-review list reviewed with the user: decisions on VF-001, VF-002, VF-018 and VF-020 recorded, VF-011 and VF-013 closed
coverage.md and jbmc-upstream.md brought up to date: extension 2 (the unwinding count per entry of a loop) is done, and VF-009 is closed
An interrupted push starts no other upload, and the integration scripts run sync.py's run-record and performance suites
collect keeps a changes.diff over jj's 1 MiB limit gzipped, or as a summary of the files it changes, for VF-020
VF-001's two conformance jobs resubmitted with mkdir -p target before the tee (verification pending)
VF-002: examples 147 and 148 resubmitted, and 149's wording corrected to the two contracts its proof rests on (verification pending)
The own checker's search for a smaller witness is bounded by work, not time, so the witness is the same on every machine (verification pending)
VF-018: a triage job that records what JBMC is given for H5's objects.Kernel#price and measures where its time goes (verification pending)
Example 148's resubmitted job no longer names three contracts in its title
The foundations streams' four run records published, and run-streams.sh copies a stream's records into the default workspace itself
Record session traces
